findings.F1: The deepest falls happen in rising months. On the book's worst 5 % of days, held bars with a positive 30-day return made 303 of 399 cases, summing −12.70 against −4.21 for those with a negative 30-day return, and the windows with the deepest book falls (w16 −30.9 %, w17 −29.7 %) are ones where the coins rose overall (summed returns +0.54 and +0.51).
findings.F2: Inside the regime, the idea's effect sits in coins already falling over 30 days. Among regime bars in the lowest quarter of 30-day return, closes near the low were followed by +1.83 % excess next day (t 3.88, n 255), against −1.18 % (t −2.28, n 212) for mid closes and −0.60 % (n 197) near the high. That lowest quarter alone averages about +0.15 %, so the falling-month condition is not an effect of its own.
findings.F3: In the highest quarter of 30-day return, closes near the low earned −0.12 % excess (n 174) while being held at the largest allocation (0.64), so the rising-month part of the book carries risk without gain.
findings.F4: The book loses on its mid-range closes, which the long-only forecast still holds at about 0.4 of the book. Regime bars with an up day and a mid close lost −0.75 % excess next day (t −2.99, n 377), and in the lowest 30-day quarter mid closes lost −1.18 %. Only the near-low third carries the rise (+0.63 %, t 2.63, n 645, on down days).
findings.F5: The effect grows with how wide the 30-day ranges are against the 90-day ones. In the widest third of the range ratio, near-low closes gained +1.40 % excess (t 2.26, n 134) against −1.41 % for mid closes, while the widest third alone averages about −0.17 %, and the mildest third shows +0.80 % near the low (t 1.52).
findings.F6: A down day explains much of the effect on its own, so it is not a repair. Regime bars after a down day earn +0.49 % excess (t 2.67, n 1291) against +0.63 % when the close is also near the low. Bars after a deep down day earn about the same with near-low closes (+1.11 %, n 318) as with mid closes (+1.06 %).
findings.F7: The size is thin against cost. The total move is +0.35 % per case against a 0.19 % trade cost (unusual move t 1.43), so the repair must come from a stronger case of the situation, as in F2 and F5, rather than from more trading.

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily high-low ranges over the past 30 days are wide compared with the past 90 days and its 30-day return is negative, the lower its close sits within the day's high-low range, the larger its rise over the next 1 day, and the more so the deeper its 30-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy closes pinned near the day's low in agitated markets only while the coin is down over the month, and stay out of such closes in rising months, where the book's deepest falls occur.
ideas.name: near-low rebound in falling months

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily high-low ranges over the past 30 days are wide compared with the past 90 days, the further its close sits below the middle of the day's high-low range, the larger its rise over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold only closes in the lower part of the day's range, sized by how far below the middle they sit, and not carry mid-range closes that lose.
ideas.name: below-midrange close rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily high-low ranges over the past 30 days are wide compared with the past 90 days, the lower its close sits within the day's high-low range, the larger its rise over the next 1 day, and the wider the past 30 days' ranges are against the past 90 days', the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the near-low rebound trade up as the month's swings widen against the quarter's, putting the book's risk where the move per case covers the trade's cost.
ideas.name: rebound scaled by range widening
